their_evidence: Missing opening stage before stage 0: in S1#16 'End of the Beginning' Hand is briefed aboard the Bus by Coulson, Garrett and Triplett, then back at the Hub shoots down Garrett's defence of the plan and orders him not to call her 'Vic'. They turn enemies in S1#17, where the existing stage sits.

stages.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S1#17
stages.text: John Garrett and Victoria Hand once served together in Lisbon, and he jokes that she is a buzzkill at parties. When he is exposed as the Clairvoyant, Hand takes him into custody to send him to the Fridge, and Grant Ward kills her on the way.
stages.on_a_card_about_b: An old colleague from Lisbon, who takes Garrett into custody.
stages.on_b_card_about_a: An old colleague from Lisbon, exposed as the Clairvoyant.

their_evidence: The Framework events in this stage (Fitz as Hydra's Doctor rejecting Radcliffe's appeal, killing Agnes Kitsworth and imprisoning Radcliffe) happen in S4#17 'Identity and Change'. The season-wide title 'S4' places the stage before S4#1, ahead of the Aida work (S4#1) and Radcliffe's exposed betrayal (S4#11) that its card lines refer to.

question: After the Framework stage (moved to S4#17), should a stage be added at S4#20 'Farewell, Cruel World!', where Radcliffe, who first helps Fitz hunt Simmons, turns on him, overpowers him and sends him back through to the real world, regretting all he has done?
options: Add an ally stage at Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S4#20: Radcliffe overpowers Fitz and sends him out of the Framework, regretting everything he has done since the Darkhold
Leave as is
their_evidence: S4#20: Fitz begins hunting Simmons with help from Radcliffe; Fitz is overpowered by Radcliffe, who regrets all his actions; Radcliffe sends Fitz through, followed by Simmons.
